strategy.thesis: Gender-smart impact fund management firm investing in growing SMEs that balance meaningful impact and financial returns, targeting climate action, livelihoods for underserved communities and gender equity aligned with the UN SDGs.

summary.en: C4D Partners (Capital 4 Development) spun out of Dutch NGO ICCO Cooperation in 2017 and is a gender-smart impact private-equity firm headquartered in Bengaluru. It closed a USD 30M C4D Asia Fund in 2018 and launched the India-dedicated USD 75M (INR 375-550 Cr) Bharat Shubharambh Fund, having made 29 social-business investments across climate resilience, financial inclusion, agribusiness and inclusive growth; 58% of investments are in women-led businesses.

strategy.thesis: Gender-lens early-growth fund investing in women-owned, women-led and women-influenced companies, with a particular emphasis on gender-equitable climate action; aims to empower 30 million women by 2030.

summary.en: AWE Funds (Achieving Women Equity), founded and led by Seema Chaturvedi, is a SEBI-registered Category II AIF gender-lens fund investing in women-owned, women-led and women-influenced companies in climate tech, healthtech, fintech and the future of work across India and the US. It secured a $15M first close, deploys $0.5M-$3M tickets, and received a Climate Gender Equity Fund (CGEF) grant to back 6-8 women-led/benefiting climate companies; its mission is to empower 30 million women by 2030.

summary.en: Upaya Social Ventures is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit impact investor (US HQ Seattle, India office Bengaluru) founded in 2011 that provides investment and support to early-stage businesses creating dignified jobs for people living in extreme poverty in India. It reports 100K+ dignified jobs created, 57 investments and 144 businesses accelerated, working across clean energy/DRE, food & agriculture, waste & circularity and textiles with an inclusive climate-action lens.

summary.en: Yunus Social Business Fund Bengaluru (YSBFB), co-founded in 2017 by Suresh Krishna and Vinitha Reddy as the India fund of the Yunus Social Business global initiative (founded by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus), is an RBI-regulated NBFC providing patient capital of Rs 50 lakh-3 crore (debt, equity, convertible/preference) to social businesses in water, sanitation, waste, livelihoods and agriculture serving India's poorest. It had invested in 69 companies as of May 2023, and was renamed Navaka Social Business Fund effective 11 Sept 2025.

summary.en: Gray Matters Capital is an Atlanta-headquartered private operating foundation (founded by Bob Pattillo) with a Bengaluru office and a strong India focus, investing through a gender lens via its coLABS and edLABS portfolios launched in 2017. It targets seed-stage enterprises improving the lives of women and girls — concentrated in education, skilling and future-of-work — with an India education budget of ~$40M over three years, and reports 75+ portfolio companies and a mission to enable education for 100 million women by 2036.

strategy.thesis: India's peer-to-peer social investment platform (RBI-regulated NBFC-P2P) channeling low-cost microloans from social investors to rural farmers, artisans and micro-entrepreneurs — over 93% of borrowers are women — working with local development agencies across 14+ states.

summary.en: Rang De is India's peer-to-peer social investment platform, operational since 2008 and RBI-regulated (as an NBFC-P2P) since 2019. It channels low-cost microloans from social investors (12,443+ to date) to rural farmers, artisans and micro-entrepreneurs across 14+ states, with 93.25% of its microloans going to women, deliberately keeping initiatives small so individual borrowers receive more support.

strategy.thesis: Non-dilutive grant fund for first-time entrepreneurs under 25 from across India, with a deliberate focus on founders outside the top metros — providing INR 20 lakh with no equity dilution plus operator-led mentorship, GTM studio and talent support.

program.eligibility: First-time entrepreneurs under the age of 25 from across India

summary.en: WTFund is a non-dilutive grant fund launched in 2024 by Zerodha co-founder Nikhil Kamath for first-time entrepreneurs under 25 from across India. It gives selected founders an INR 20 lakh grant with no equity dilution plus operator-led mentorship, a GTM studio and talent support; with a deliberate long-tail/non-metro focus — ~60% of applications come from smaller towns and more than half of funded startups are based outside India's top metros. Since launch it has received 5,000+ applications across 50+ cities.

summary.en: Pioneering Ventures is a Zurich- and Mumbai-based venture accelerator that floated a $70M private-equity Rural India Impact Fund (raising mainly from European institutional and family offices) to invest in India's agriculture and food sector.
